I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Negative Appraisals.value: I can't stop bad things from happening to me
I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me

issues.explanation: The trigger set is mostly coherent with rape trauma (locked/confined spaces, sexual-violence comments), but sirens are hard to connect to the rest of this profile and trauma context. With strong Negative Appraisals↔Threat and links from both to Triggers, the triggers should plausibly cue the patient's threat meanings; sirens do not fit the sexual-assault/confinement theme represented by the other trigger and appraisal items.

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: Within Threat, hypervigilant unsafe-world items (back to wall, staying alert to sleep) fit well, but 'taking too many risks' pulls in the opposite direction and is hard to reconcile with the same immediate threat style. It also lacks support elsewhere in the profile, since no other items suggest disinhibition, anger, numbing, or self-destructive coping.

vignette:
Kwame, a 37-year-old psychologist, found himself trapped in a life that felt increasingly suffocating. The traumatic event that forever altered his perception of safety occurred two years ago when he was attacked in a dimly lit parking garage after a late session. The experience haunted him both in waking life and in his dreams, replaying with a vividness that left him breathless. Since that night, Kwame felt as though he had been stripped of his autonomy, and he began to view the world through a lens of hopelessness. This pervasive sense of vulnerability led Kwame to interpret every experience as a potential threat, reinforcing his belief that he was always on the brink of danger. His negative appraisals shaped his perception of the world; he began to believe that he was a target for harm, which made every unfamiliar face seem like a potential threat waiting to emerge. Having decided that he was permanently vulnerable, he walked into rooms already braced - the threat arrived with him before anything had happened. This belief that he was always at risk made Kwame hyper-aware of potential dangers, reinforcing his perception that the world was filled with threats lurking around every corner. He was convinced that he would never truly feel safe again, and this belief seeped into every corner of his existence, shaping his reality in ways he could hardly articulate.

Kwame's days were punctuated by moments that served as painful reminders of his trauma. He dreaded being in confined spaces, such as the small office where he often met clients. The pervasive sense of threat he carried with him made even ordinary situations feel charged with potential danger, turning the familiar into a minefield of anxiety that set his heart racing. His heightened sense of threat made even ordinary situations feel charged with danger, transforming the mundane into a source of anxiety that he could not escape. The sensation of being locked in made his heart race, and he would find himself scanning the room, hyper-aware of the exits. Comments on sexual violence, whether in the media or casual conversations, would send shivers down his spine, triggering a cascade of memories that made him feel powerless. These reminders were amplified by the ever-present threat he felt, as they reminded him of the danger that had invaded his life, making each comment feel like an imminent risk to his safety. He avoided situations where he might find himself alone with men, as the mere thought of it filled him with an acute sense of vulnerability. This heightened sense of threat meant that even benign encounters were fraught with worry, causing him to perceive danger in moments that others would view as harmless. The conviction that he was exposed to others, that they could somehow perceive the darkness he carried within, only deepened his isolation. He often felt as if he wore a visible scar, one that marked him as a victim, forever altering how he interacted with those around him.

The threat of danger loomed large in Kwame's mind. He could not relax, even in the comfort of his own home. Sleep eluded him, as he lay wide awake, the weight of alertness pressing down on him like a physical burden. He had come to believe that unless his back was against a wall, he was vulnerable to attack, a constant reminder of the helplessness he felt. This hyper-vigilance fed into his negative appraisals, reinforcing the narrative that he had no future worth looking forward to. The constant sense of danger became the most convincing evidence for Kwame that his life had changed irreparably, leading him to believe that he would always be vulnerable and never truly safe. Each moment of dread reinforced his negative beliefs, confirming that he was not the kind of person who could ever feel secure in this world. Every moment of dread confirmed his deepest fears, solidifying a narrative that he was not the kind of person who got to feel safe, and this pervasive belief weighed heavily on his spirit. Feeling this afraid all the time, he had eventually come to accept the conclusion his body kept offering: that he was not the kind of person who got to feel safe. The world seemed fraught with peril, and he felt that no matter how hard he tried, he could not stop bad things from happening to him. This constant awareness of danger confirmed his deepest fears, solidifying his negative appraisals that he was destined to live in a world where safety was an illusion. It was as if the universe conspired against him, and he was left helpless in the face of that reality.

Kwame's professional life began to suffer as well. He found it increasingly difficult to maintain the empathy required to be an effective psychologist. His clients spoke of their struggles, but he could barely focus; all he could think about was his own turmoil. He began to withdraw from social engagements, fearing that others might inadvertently draw attention to his trauma. His friends, once a source of comfort, now felt like reminders of his inadequacies, reinforcing his belief that he was exposed and vulnerable. This sense of detachment from others only exacerbated his feelings of hopelessness, trapping him in a spiral where every negative thought fed into another.

As the months turned into years, Kwame found himself at a crossroads. The realization that he could no longer bear the weight of his trauma alone brought him to this moment of seeking help. In the solitude of his office, he sat with his thoughts, wrestling with the fear that seeking therapy might expose him further, that he would have to confront the very memories he fought so hard to suppress. Yet, there was a flicker of hope buried beneath the despair, a yearning to reclaim the life he once led. Kwame hoped that through therapy, he might find a way to navigate the darkness, to build a future where he could feel secure in his own skin again. What frightened him most was the thought that he might always feel this way, trapped in a cycle of fear and helplessness, unable to escape the shadows of his past.
